subject: Performance SLO: Context window & token limits — follow-up (FinCo)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: John Lee <john.lee@finco.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 15:22:00 -0000
Subject: Follow-up: Performance SLO / context window discussion (FinCo)

Thanks for the time today, John — great discussion. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- Summary of what we heard from FinCo: you need the model to support up to a 120k token input (documents + metadata) for single-request context, produce up to 4k tokens of output for summaries, and keep 95th percentile latency under 2.5s for interactive use.
- Typical concurrency: spikes to ~80 concurrent users during batch review windows; baseline steady-state concurrency ~10 QPS.
- Streaming: you indicated streaming is preferred for UX (incremental summary updates) but final output must be complete within the SLO.

Open clarifying questions for FinCo to confirm (so we can size Dedicated capacity / tests):
1) For the 120k token context, what percentage of requests are actually that large vs. typical average size? (ballpark %)
2) Are you expecting KV cache reuse between requests (same user/session providing follow-ups) or are requests mostly independent?
3) For streaming, do you need per-token latency below X (if you have a number) or just end-to-end 95p under 2.5s?

Proposed next steps from Redwood:
- We'll run a sizing test with our runtime that simulates 120k token prompts at varying output lengths (500/2k/4k tokens) to measure latency and throughput.
- Vivek will propose a test harness and rough instance sizing by EOD tomorrow.
- We'll share a perf plan and a sample latency report (attachment) after the first run.

Attaching: redwood_perf_plan_v1.pdf (test plan + metrics we will capture). Also added a template sheet (finco_latency_requirements.xlsx) for you to fill in real traffic percentiles if you have them.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: John Lee <john.lee@finco.com>

Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finco.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 18:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance SLO / context window discussion (FinCo)

Hi Marissa — thanks, that captures it well. A few answers inline: 

1) 120k token requests are heavy, maybe ~5% of traffic (these are full historical audits). Typical request size ~8-12k tokens (majority).
2) We do expect some session-level reuse: reviewers will ask follow-ups within a session ~30% of the time. KV cache reuse would be valuable.
3) Streaming: primary UX expectation is progressive rendering — we care about the first bytes showing up quickly (sub-1s ideal) but the hard SLO is end-to-end 95p < 2.5s for interactive flows. For batch exports, higher latency is acceptable.

We don't have exact concurrency percentiles yet — Priya is pulling historical reviewer logs and will drop them into your sheet.

Also, for security/compliance: we need details on data-at-rest encryption and audit logs for these tests since we'll want to run an initial PoC on our staging environment. Can Vivek loop in a short note on the approach for a staging test?

Thanks,
John Lee
Director of AI Products | FinCo
john.lee@finco.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 02:10:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance SLO / context window discussion (FinCo)

Hi John — quick technical note on staging PoC and test harness: 

1) Data & security: for staging runs we can deploy Redwood Private in your VPC or run on a short-lived Private instance with customer-managed KMS so keys never leave your environment. All test artifacts (logs, traces) can be forwarded to your audit bucket. We'll provide an SOC2-friendly checklist before tests.

2) Test plan & metrics: we'll simulate traffic with a hybrid workload: 5% 120k-token, 30% 8-12k, 65% <5k. For each class we will vary output targets (500/2k/4k tokens) and measure: 50/90/95/99 latency per token and end-to-end, CPU/GPU utilization, memory, and KV cache hit rates.

3) Runtime optimizations that matter for large context windows: 
- KV cache reuse across a session reduces repeated encoding work.
- Prefix caching for common doc headers.
- Chunked attention and offloading for very long contexts (we may prefer a streaming generation with incremental attention windows).

4) Expected trade-offs: at 120k tokens, end-to-end 95p under 2.5s for 4k token output is unlikely on a single GPU unless we accept very aggressive quantization and model distillation — more realistic is a multi-GPU sharded setup with optimized kernels (we'll run benchmark and provide numbers). For your interactive SLOs we recommend: 
- Configure KV/session cache + per-request windowing so that typical interactive requests hit much lower effective context size,
- Use model variant tuned for throughput with streaming enabled for first-byte latency,
- Provision Dedicated capacity with burst headroom for spikes to 80 concurrent users.

I'll attach a short checklist and expected instance sizing after the first full run. Planning to start smoke tests tomorrow morning (US).

— Vivek
